variables.name: grid/columns
variables.description: Column count, 12 — UX4G/Bootstrap. Divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6, which is the whole reason 12 is the near-universal choice. Carbon's 16 (dropping to 8 and 4 at smaller breakpoints) is more expressive but would break UX4G parity for no gain the estate can use.

variables.name: grid/gutter
variables.description: The gap BETWEEN columns — 24px, UX4G/Bootstrap's 1.5rem exactly. Bootstrap applies half either side of each column; bind this as the layout grid's gutter and let the implementation split it.

variables.name: grid/margin/mobile
variables.description: Use for the page’s side margin on a phone — the gap between the layout grid and the viewport edge. Bind it to the frame’s horizontal padding, not to the grid’s gutter, which is `grid/gutter`.

variables.name: grid/margin/tablet
variables.description: Use for the page’s side margin on a tablet — the gap between the layout grid and the viewport edge. Bind it to the frame’s horizontal padding, not to the grid’s gutter, which is `grid/gutter`.

variables.name: grid/margin/desktop
variables.description: Use for the page’s side margin on a desktop — the gap between the layout grid and the viewport edge. Bind it to the frame’s horizontal padding, not to the grid’s gutter, which is `grid/gutter`.

variables.name: layout/bar/height
variables.description: The government accessibility bar. Genuinely fixed: it carries one row of controls at a known size, in every surface and every locale.

variables.name: layout/flag/width
variables.description: The Indian flag mark in the accessibility bar. Fixed so the bar's left edge is identical across the estate.

variables.name: layout/masthead/minHeight
variables.description: The brand row's MINIMUM, not its height. It hugs its content, which varies: two or three lines of ministry lockup, an optional BETA badge, a search field on the website, an account block on portals. 72 is the floor that keeps the emblem legible when the lockup is shortest. Never lay out against a fixed masthead height — see `layout/chrome/minHeight`.

variables.name: layout/chrome/minHeight
variables.description: Accessibility bar plus brand row at their minimum — the offset the sidebar and content start at on a portal page. Use it for a scroll anchor or a sticky offset, NOT to size the shell: the brand row hugs, so the real value moves with the content. AppShell lays the shell out as a three-row grid (`auto auto 1fr`) so nothing subtracts this from the viewport. At the documented content the navbar measures 134 including its shadow, of which 118 is the layout box.

variables.name: layout/sidebar/width
variables.description: The portal sidebar's expanded width. Genuinely fixed: the nav labels are known copy, and a fluid sidebar would move the content edge on every route. Its inner padding is `padding/m` (16), leaving a 268 item column; items are `target/spacious` (48) tall. Below the tablet breakpoint the sidebar is not narrowed — it becomes a drawer.

variables.name: layout/login/hero/width
variables.description: Desktop hero column carrying the portal photograph, brand lockup and the signing-into bar.

variables.name: layout/login/panel/width
variables.description: Desktop auth form panel. 1440 - 922 = 518.

variables.name: layout/login/panel/gutter
variables.description: Horizontal inset of the form panel and the hero content. The space scale jumps 32 -> 120, so this sits between them deliberately.

variables.name: layout/login/content/width
variables.description: The form content column itself. 518 - 2x64 = 390. Every auth field, button and divider is this wide.

variables.name: layout/tab/indicator
variables.description: Thickness of the selected tab's underline or rail. Deliberately NOT `control/border/width`: this is a selection mark that happens to be a line, not a control edge, so it must not move when the form-control hairline is retuned.

variables.name: layout/tab/track
variables.description: Inset between an enclosed track and the pills inside it — the track's own padding, and the indicator's top/bottom inset. Small enough that the track reads as a frame around the pills rather than a panel containing them.

variables.name: target/min
variables.description: The absolute floor — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA. Use ONLY where the spacing exception is genuinely satisfied or the target is inline in a sentence. Anything a citizen must hit on a phone deserves `comfortable`.

variables.name: target/comfortable
variables.description: WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), Level AAA, and Apple's Human Interface Guidelines minimum (44pt). The right default for a public government service: it clears the AA floor with room to spare and matches what iOS users' fingers are calibrated to.

variables.name: target/spacious
variables.description: Material Design 3 / Android's minimum touch target (48dp). Use for primary actions and anything used one-handed on the move — this is the largest of the three published floors, so meeting it satisfies all of them.

variables.name: target/spacing
variables.description: Minimum gap BETWEEN adjacent targets — Material 3's 8dp separation. It is also what makes WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception reachable: separation, not size, is what stops a 24px target being mis-tapped.

variables.name: cmp/badge/dotSize
variables.description: The status/unread DOT — ONE definition for the whole estate, not one per component. Bound by the Badge's dot and by Tabs' badge; when this moves, every dot moves. It is 6 and not the on-grid 8 on purpose: beside 14px label text an 8px dot reads as a bullet rather than a signal, and 6 is what Material and Carbon both publish. A literal rather than an alias because no ref/size step is 6, and inventing one would add a scale step for a single affordance — the same reasoning layout/bar/height (46) and layout/flag/width (33) already follow. Authored in Figma first; reconciled into code 2026-08-18.

variables.name: cmp/badge/dotSizeLg
variables.description: The dot beside 16px body text — Badge size=lg, and Tabs size=L. A dot is sized against the TYPE it annotates, not against its container, which is why this steps with the type scale and not with the control height.

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/height
variables.description: Bar height. ALIASES 46px rather than repeating 46px — until 2026-08-18 both carried the literal independently, so moving one silently left the other behind. layout/bar/height is the published Figma name the master binds to; this is the component-scoped handle the CSS uses.

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/flagWidth
variables.description: Flag/emblem chip width. ALIASES 33px rather than repeating 33px — same duplicate-literal defect as `height`, fixed 2026-08-18. Height is 1.375rem, making a 3:2 chip.

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/flagHeight

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/pillSize

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/stepSize

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/launchIconSize

variables.name: cmp/accessibilityBar/iconButtonSize

variables.name: border/neutral/subtle
variables.description: Use for a hairline that separates without drawing the eye — dividers and card edges. Contrast 1.35:1 vs bg/neutral/base — BELOW the ≥3:1 implied by the “subtle” rung.

variables.name: border/neutral/base
variables.description: Use for a standard boundary. Contrast 1.66:1 vs bg/neutral/base — no guaranteed contrast class; treat as a boundary, not as text.

variables.name: border/neutral/bolder/default
variables.description: Use for the visible edge of an interactive control, such as an input or a checkbox. Contrast 3.06:1 vs bg/neutral/base — BELOW the ≥4.5:1 implied by the “bolder” rung.

variables.name: border/neutral/inverse/default
variables.description: Border/rule ink on a dark or brand surface — the inverse of border/neutral/base. Nested as inverse/default rather than a bare `inverse` leaf because it has a `subtle` sibling, which is the same shape border/neutral/bolder already uses (bolder/default, bolder/hover).

variables.name: border/neutral/inverse/subtle
variables.description: The quieter inverse rule — white at 40%, pre-composited so consumers never hand-roll an opacity. Used by Divider Tone=Inverse subtle and the AccessibilityBar's separators. The Figma variable was `border/neutral/inverse-subtle` until 2026-08-18 — a hyphen inside a segment, which grammar RULE 1 forbids; renamed IN PLACE so bindings followed. Contrast 3.81:1 vs bg/neutral/inverse — meets ≥3:1: UI boundaries, icons, non-text (WCAG 1.4.11).

variables.name: bg/neutral/base
variables.description: Use for the ordinary, quietest fill — page and card surfaces that must not compete with their content.

variables.name: bg/neutral/subtler
variables.description: Use for a barely-there tint, for hovered rows and zebra striping. Contrast 1.14:1 vs bg/neutral/base — no guaranteed contrast class; treat as a fill, not as text.

variables.name: text/neutral/bolder
variables.description: Use for max-contrast headings that need to outrank surrounding text. Contrast 18.94:1 vs bg/neutral/base — meets ≥4.5:1: max-contrast headings (WCAG 1.4.3 AA).

variables.name: text/link/brand/default
variables.description: Text-link colour. Decoupled from action.primary so it can be lighter on dark surfaces (≥4.5:1 as text) without weakening white-on-primary button contrast. Contrast 4.64:1 vs bg/neutral/base — meets ≥4.5:1: text (WCAG 1.4.3 AA).

variables.name: focus/ring
variables.description: Use for the focus indicator. WCAG 2.4.7 makes this non-optional — never suppress it, and never substitute a colour with less contrast.

variables.name: overlay/neutral/boldest
variables.description: Use for the scrim behind a modal or drawer — it suppresses the page beneath rather than carrying content.

variables.name: overlay/brand/hover

variables.name: ref/font/family/display
variables.description: The optical Display cut, for the 40-80px Display ramp. Noto Sans ships two cuts of one design: the text cut is drawn for reading at 12-24px, and at 80px its open spacing reads as loose. The Display cut tightens it. This is now genuinely LOADED (apps/hub root layout, weight 500) — for a long time it was named here and loaded nowhere, so it fell through to the text cut and the matching Figma variable could not resolve at all. LATIN ONLY: `Noto Sans Display` has no Devanagari subset and `Noto Sans Devanagari` has no Display cut, so a Hindi heading falls through to Noto Sans by design. In Figma the same cut is a STYLE of Noto Sans ("Display Medium"), not a family — see design.md. Raw type step. variables.name: ref/font/family/mono
variables.description: CODE AND TECHNICAL STRINGS ONLY — token names, CSS snippets, file paths in the design-system docs. NOT for numbers, amounts or reference numbers: those want `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on Noto Sans, which aligns digits down a column while keeping them in the same typeface as the text beside them. Switching a data column to a monospace face is the clumsier fix and looks like a different design. The estate already does this correctly in the Aadhaar/PAN field, the charts, the SLA indicator and the shared DataTable. DELIBERATELY a system stack: `ui-monospace` resolves to the platform's own mono (SF Mono, Cascadia, Roboto Mono) — all well-drawn, all disambiguating 0/O and 1/l/I, and already on the device. A webfont here would download on every page to style sample code on a handful of documentation pages, which on a low-bandwidth government audience is not a trade worth making. IBM Plex Mono was set here briefly and reverted for that reason. Raw type step. Prefer a text style from the Display / Headline / Title / Body / Label ramp — these are the parts those styles are assembled from.

variables.name: ref/breakpoint/desktopXl
variables.description: The fourth anchor — where the content cap widens from `container/content` (1200) to `container/contentXl` (1320). UX4G states the two widths as guidance ("max content width: 1200px desktop, 1320px desktop XL") without publishing a breakpoint, so the anchor comes from the estate's own viewport ladder, where desktop is 1440 and desktop-XL is 1768. Bootstrap's `container-xxl` engages at 1400 and was rejected for this: at 1400 the 1440 design frame would take the 1320 cap, contradicting the 1200-at-desktop guidance and the website Handoff, which shows the wide margin of a 1200 column at 1440. UX4G's Bootstrap CONTAINER LADDER is a separate thing and is kept faithfully as `container/sm`…`container/2xl`; this token governs the CONTENT CAP only. Not part of the type curve either — `clamp()` still tops out at 1280, so this anchor resizes no glyph. Viewport anchor. The fluid type curve is built from these; they are not a layout property to bind.

variables.name: container/2xl
variables.description: Completes UX4G's container ladder, which is Bootstrap's: 540 / 720 / 960 / 1140 / 1320. It was the one step missing here, so `contentXl` had to restate the literal; it now aliases this.

variables.name: container/content
variables.description: The desktop content cap. Changed from 1280px to UX4G 3.0's published 1200px on 13 August 2026 ('Grid and layout': max content width 1200px desktop, 1320px desktop XL). Until then the estate ran FOUR widths at once — this token said 1280 and nothing consumed it, 22 website section files hardcoded the same 1280 as a literal, SiteHeader defaulted to 1320, and PortalLoginShell's chrome used 1536. The visible defect was that above 1320px the masthead's content ran 20px wider each side than the page beneath it, so the National Emblem did not line up with the content column. At the 1440 design frame 1200 leaves a 120px margin either side, comfortably clear of the 32px `grid/margin/desktop` floor.

variables.name: container/contentXl
variables.description: The content cap above `breakpoint/desktopXl`. Aliases `container/2xl` rather than restating 1320, so the estate's cap and UX4G's ladder cannot drift apart. UX4G publishes the value but not the point at which it engages; Bootstrap — whose ladder UX4G's is — engages `container-xxl` at 1400, so that is the anchor.

variables.name: container/narrow
variables.description: AccessibilityBar narrow content container (Figma layout/container/narrow). Same 720px as container.md, named for the bar's own Layout variant.

variables.name: container/wide
variables.description: AccessibilityBar wide content container (Figma layout/container/wide). 1200px is the Figma master's own value. It now COINCIDES with `container/content`, which moved 1280 > 1200 on 13 August 2026, but is deliberately left as a literal rather than aliased: the two are independent decisions that happen to agree today — this one is the bar's Figma master, that one is UX4G's published desktop cap — and aliasing would silently drag the bar along if the page cap moves again.
